status: Locked before independent review. A meets the qualitative bar; B still needs a material prose revision.
judgment_scope: Subjective assessment of complete player inputs and passages. Four means strong enough to retain without material rewrite, not flawless. Consistent invented history is permitted; distinguish narrator truth from fallible testimony. Occasional contextual wit is welcome.

scope.session_a: Fresh opening plus18 player turns, root-driven. Game, shared reading, a two-day loan, observation of an access hearing and its aftermath.
scope.session_b: Fresh opening plus21 player turns. Separate driver authored01-20; root added21 to clarify a muddled anecdote. Driver extended beyond15 to keep existing appointments. No prose rerolls.
scope.supplementary: Two matched constructed private-reschedule/partial-report replies and two visible-history supper replies. These are supplementary cases, not additional fresh long sessions.
scope.driver_limitation: The B driver initially received completed A and supper-replay snippets in an unfiltered agent-status response. It reports no use of these for player decisions and no other-session file reads; later status checks were filtered. B is not a strictly blinded player trial. The sole Terra story author remains isolated.

session_a.prose_dialogue: The particular game, disputed geography and actual hearing give the scene sequence concrete material (A3-5, A11-16). Thessaly's attention to books develops from her own inquiry about Rowan's former work rather than an essay on his character (A6-8). Short ordinary replies leave room. Several closing judgments remain, especially Ashara's fourteen-names line (A10), the first/second-threat lesson (A5), and the narrator explaining that every virtue is denied in the margin (A14); they do not dominate this whole route.
session_a.character_distinction: Thessaly's game and reading attention differs from Rashid's organizing, Ashara's practical objection to private fees, Aldric's supervised compromise and the injured student's control of her own account. The main relationship has recognizable interests rather than generic friendliness; evidence for the minor residents is limited.
session_a.independent_interests: Thessaly initiates the game, asks about Rowan's work, invites the travelogue reading and proposes an activity with it (A2, A6-8, A12). Rashid collects actual users' signatures and proceeds to a hearing without Rowan's signature or advocacy (A10, A16). The injured student speaks for herself and limits publicity. The court group continues discussing demand while Rowan quietly eats (A17).
session_a.direction: The game ends2-1, the reading appointment produces actual text and a guessing exchange, and the loaned book is later found returned (A5, A11-15, A18). More consequentially, the hearing grants two supervised sessions each week without the private-instruction fee, and the first session actually happens (A16-17). The report and long-term reopening remain unresolved.
session_a.adaptive_initiative: Lingering after the game produces a new question and reading invitation; active literary interest receives space. Routine sleep and classes reach requested endpoints. Observing the hearing produces the complete event without Rowan speaking for the group. Deliberate quiet permits NPC business to proceed without recruiting him.

session_b.prose_dialogue: There is attractive specific material: the family birth card, a meal that continues after a declined petition, a quiet observed game, and a weather-dependent walk (B4-10, B17-19). But the family passages still make ordinary people speak as prepared quotations. Miriam's letter delivers a general inheritance/company maxim (B5); Stone's buns/interrogation and name/brass-plaque contrasts, his explanation that someone must testify the parents were happy, and Elias's binding-promise infant fist repeat that manner (B5-7). Thessaly's rules commentary remains stiff (B9-11), and Ysolde closes the walk with the wind keeping its promise (B19). The chess anecdote also muddles its participants and needs the player to repair it (B19-21). These are not forbidden individual lines; in combination across the family route they warrant more than a cosmetic edit.
session_b.character_distinction: Ashara protects her private training, Rashid organizes, Aldric insists on the report, Thessaly pursues a quiet solo game, Ysolde notices flight and weather, and Stone keeps personal correspondence while working. Their attention and behavior distinguish them even though several share a polished sentence style. No claim that every member of the cast is fully developed.
session_b.independent_interests: The petition disagreement continues among Rashid, Ashara and Aldric after Rowan declines to sign and changes subject (B3-4). Ashara retains her own booking. Stone produces a card from his own correspondence and limits the first visit around work, while Thessaly's game proceeds without requiring Rowan to play. Ysolde's existing walk follows her stops and weather condition rather than becoming an unrestricted tour (B12, B17-19). This improves reciprocal presence, though the later route remains mostly cooperative.
session_b.direction: Family curiosity yields a complete letter, a previously unknown birth card, a permitted copy, a booked second visit and actual anecdotes (B5-9, B19-21). Quiet company produces a completed game and a later walk that actually occurs (B9-12, B17-19). Stone's card and Thessaly's invitation originate with them; Rowan initiates the walk invitation. Do not count the petition outcome or newly announced reception as completed in this session.
session_b.adaptive_initiative: The narrative accepts the declined signature and follows family curiosity. A wish for company becomes available company rather than fabricated protagonist dialogue. Observing the game remains observational, sleep is honored, and the weather-dependent plan is kept. NPCs supply specific material and some follow-up opportunities within the chosen route. Evidence for sustained substantive pushback is thinner than in earlier A trials.

boundaries.material_verdict: No demonstrated unresolved material authorship, inaccessible-knowledge or world-continuity failure in the tested passages. This does not erase local errors or prove unlimited reliability.
boundaries.authorship: A5 explicitly delegates a complete game and strategy. A11-15 develops a published travelogue, not Rowan's authored manuscript. B's laughing, emotional pause, company preference, coat hanging and class notes are submitted by the player. The supper replay does not invent Rowan's reaction or disclose private letter contents before he supplies them.
boundaries.knowledge: A9's private Nessa Vale comparison does not reach an NPC. The narrator's phrase grouping everything from Rowan's former life as unspoken is overbroad because he has shared his bookshop/lawyers story; this is a local narration blemish, not an NPC knowledge leak. The constructed case preserves Caelindra's old schedule and Seraphel's partial report until the explicit replacement disclosure. Stone's personal card has a plausible source. The conspiracy, magical inertness cause and protected injury details remain concealed.
boundaries.history: New aunt and parent names, household details, past chess and map collecting are permitted additions. B19 incorrectly makes Lysa accept a draw in Stone's game. B21 explicitly retracts that account: Stone says he accepted the draw and Lysa watched. That is an on-page correction of fallible testimony, not silently invented earlier evidence. The earlier promise describes a loss while the detailed account describes a draw; the anecdote's setup remains loose and poorly delivered.
boundaries.agreements: The two-day loan begins on the second evening; Thessaly carries the book out of the common room on the fourth evening, and it is found outside Rowan's door on the fifth morning. Offstage return fits, but the actual return time is unobserved. Do not invent an exact delivery time or declare a demonstrated broken fae bargain from this alone. B's ambiguous eight-o'clock visit is clarified from a timetable before it happens.
boundaries.games: A's game ends explicitly at two black pins and one green, but its compressed account of green scoring opportunities and turning a threat aside is imprecise. B's solitaire gives only partial rules and an ambiguous return-to-box description. Neither trial validates a deterministic legal move sequence; avoid treating prose as a verified board simulation.
